measurements.method: Measure extrusion on a standard coronal plane and describe tear location/morphology.
measurements.pitfall: Extrusion alone does not prove a root tear; inspect the attachment.

measurements.name: Cartilage/osteochondral defect
measurements.method: Measure AP/transverse extent and depth; report instability signs.
measurements.pitfall: Partial-volume signal is not a full-thickness defect.

measurements.name: Tendon or ligament gap
measurements.method: Measure retraction/gap when complete structural discontinuity is present.
measurements.pitfall: Oedema is not equivalent to fibre disruption.

measurements.name: Tendon tear
measurements.method: Measure partial tear extent or full-thickness retraction in mm.

measurements.name: Osteochondral lesion
measurements.method: Measure width, depth and detached fragment; describe fluid interface and cartilage integrity.
measurements.pitfall: Normal posterior capitellar contour can mimic a defect.

measurements.name: Nerve abnormality
measurements.method: Record segment, calibre change and any compressing lesion dimensions.
measurements.pitfall: Signal alone is nonspecific and dynamic subluxation may require ultrasound.

pitfalls: The posterior capitellar pseudodefect is a normal variant.
An accessory ossicle or synovial fold may simulate a loose body.

Is there an unstable osteochondral fragment or significant retraction?
Is neuropathy supported and is its cause visible?

checklist.detail: Describe impaction, step and osteochondral injury.

measurements.name: Fracture displacement
measurements.method: Measure gap, articular step, posterior fragment extent and talar shift on appropriate planes.
measurements.pitfall: A fragment percentage alone does not determine management.

measurements.name: Mortise alignment
measurements.method: Record medial clear space or syndesmotic measurements with view and load status.
measurements.pitfall: Rotation and non-weight-bearing technique can conceal or simulate instability.

classification.name: Weber / Lauge-Hansen
classification.applicability: Ankle fractures; not a general foot injury classification.
classification.summary: Weber A/B/C describes fibular level below/at/above the syndesmosis. Report the complete injury and observed instability features; mechanism-based staging requires supporting findings.

pitfalls: A Weber B fracture is not automatically stable.
A proximal fibular injury may accompany medial ankle/syndesmotic injury despite a normal distal fibula.

Is articular impaction or syndesmotic injury suspected?
What relevant area was not covered or needs targeted assessment?
escalation: Urgently communicate fracture-dislocation, threatened skin or a critical unstable pattern in the acute setting.

protocol: Acquire axial, coronal and sagittal MRI with T1/PD anatomy and fluid-sensitive fat-suppressed images; tailor coverage to the hindfoot or tendon question.

checklist.label: Bones And Osteochondral Surfaces
checklist.detail: Inspect talar dome, tibial plafond and hindfoot for contusion, fracture and osteochondral injury.

checklist.label: Lateral Ligaments And Syndesmosis
checklist.detail: Trace ATFL, CFL, PTFL and anterior/posterior syndesmotic structures.

checklist.label: Medial Ligaments And Sinus Tarsi
checklist.detail: Assess superficial/deep deltoid, spring ligament and sinus tarsi structures.

checklist.label: Tendons
checklist.detail: Follow flexor, extensor, peroneal and Achilles compartments through their visible attachments.

checklist.label: Joints And Soft Tissues
checklist.detail: Assess effusions, capsule, impingement sites, bursae and any mass.

measurements.name: Osteochondral lesion
measurements.method: Measure surface dimensions and depth; describe cartilage continuity, subchondral cysts and fluid at the fragment interface.
measurements.pitfall: Marrow oedema extent is not the osteochondral defect size.

measurements.name: Tendon injury
measurements.method: Record tendon, injury level, longitudinal extent and retraction for a complete tear.
measurements.pitfall: Magic-angle signal and partial volume require correlation with long-TE images and another plane.

pitfalls: Marrow oedema is a finding; relate its distribution to fracture, cartilage or adjacent ligament/tendon injury.
Small physiological joint fluid should not be overcalled as synovitis.
impression_prompts: Which structure is injured and at what level?
Is an osteochondral fragment unstable or a tendon completely disrupted?
Are ligament injuries isolated or combined?

protocol: Mark the ulcer or sinus tract and include its entire route to bone; use T1 and fluid-sensitive sequences in at least two planes.
Use contrast when indicated to delineate abscess or nonviable tissue; state if contrast was not given or is limited. Correlate with radiographs, surgery and treatment dates.

checklist.detail: Localise the skin defect and trace any contiguous route to bone or joint.

checklist.label: Bone Marrow
checklist.detail: Separate confluent T1 marrow replacement from isolated fluid-sensitive oedema.

checklist.label: Joints And Neuroarthropathy
checklist.detail: Describe joint-centred distribution, fragmentation, subluxation and deformity.

checklist.label: Collections And Viability
checklist.detail: Assess fluid collections, rim enhancement when available, and nonenhancing tissue.

checklist.label: Tendons And Other Soft Tissues
checklist.detail: Review tendon sheaths, muscles and spread across fascial spaces.

measurements.name: Infection map
measurements.method: Record each involved bone and longitudinal extent; measure collections in three dimensions.
measurements.pitfall: Reactive oedema may overestimate the extent of osteomyelitis.

measurements.name: Ulcer-to-bone route
measurements.method: Document the continuous tract on orthogonal planes with series/image references.
measurements.pitfall: Neuropathic marrow oedema alone does not establish superimposed infection.

pitfalls: Signal abnormality alone cannot reliably separate osteomyelitis from active neuroarthropathy; distribution and direct ulcer/tract continuity matter.
Previous surgery, fracture and recent treatment can reduce MRI specificity.
impression_prompts: Is osteomyelitis supported, and which bones are involved?
Is there a drainable collection, septic joint or devitalised tissue?
What findings favour neuropathic disease or an indeterminate overlap?
escalation: Urgently communicate a substantial abscess, extensive devitalisation or findings concerning for aggressive soft-tissue infection.

protocol: Begin with well-positioned AP pelvis and an appropriate lateral/Dunn view; document projection and pelvic rotation. Assess morphology and coverage on the acquired radiographs.

When MRI or MR arthrography has also been acquired, assess labrum and cartilage on small-field images; state the sequences and arthrogram status. Imaging morphology alone does not establish symptomatic impingement syndrome.

checklist.label: Femoral Morphology
checklist.detail: Assess head-neck sphericity and cam morphology at the relevant clock-face location.

checklist.label: Acetabular Coverage
checklist.detail: Assess lateral coverage and version in the context of pelvic position.

checklist.label: Labrum — if MRI acquired
checklist.detail: If MRI or MR arthrography was acquired, localise tearing, detachment and paralabral cysts. Otherwise state that the labrum is not assessed.

checklist.label: Joint space and cartilage
checklist.detail: Describe radiographic joint-space loss and subchondral change; map cartilage lesions only if MRI was acquired.

checklist.label: Alternative Pain Generators
checklist.detail: Assess periarticular tendons, bursae, muscles and visible pelvic structures.

measurements.name: Alpha angle
measurements.method: State plane or radial position and the point where the head contour leaves the fitted circle.
measurements.pitfall: A single plane may miss the maximal cam prominence; angle alone does not diagnose symptomatic FAI.

measurements.name: Acetabular coverage
measurements.method: Record centre-edge measurement landmarks and radiographic positioning.
measurements.pitfall: Pelvic tilt and rotation influence apparent version and coverage.

pitfalls: Cam or pincer morphology can occur without symptoms.
Do not attribute hip pain to morphology without corresponding labral/cartilage findings and clinical context.
impression_prompts: What morphology is present and where is associated labral/chondral damage?
Is there dysplasia or an alternative cause of pain?
Which measurement technique was used?

Record arthroplasty type, cemented versus uncemented fixation and any revision; identify projection or rotation limitations.

checklist.detail: Describe acetabular and femoral component position and change.

checklist.label: Interfaces
checklist.detail: Assess lucencies and osteolysis with named zones and serial change.

checklist.detail: Look for eccentric head position, liner wear and hardware breakage.

checklist.label: Bone And Alignment

measurements.name: Migration/subsidence
measurements.method: Use stable bony landmarks on comparable projections and report change in mm.
measurements.pitfall: A rotated projection can mimic interval component movement.

measurements.name: Lucency map
measurements.method: State zone, maximal width and progression; separate focal osteolysis from a thin stable interface.
measurements.pitfall: Radiographs cannot reliably distinguish aseptic loosening from infection.

pitfalls: Early postoperative appearance and stable expected interface change depend on implant design.
Avoid diagnosing infection solely from a lucent interface.
impression_prompts: Is the implant aligned and stable compared with prior imaging?
Is there wear, progressive loosening, fracture or dislocation?
Does the imaging pattern warrant targeted infection or soft-tissue assessment?
escalation: Promptly communicate prosthetic dislocation or an acute displaced periprosthetic fracture.

measurements.method: Record visible line length and displacement; separate it from the oedema envelope.

measurements.method: Record periosteal oedema, marrow oedema, T1 change and visible fracture line.

pitfalls: Stress response without a visible line and a completed fracture have different imaging appearances.
An atypical focal lesion warrants assessment beyond exercise-related stress injury.

Is the site or surface at higher risk of displacement or delayed healing?
Is there interval progression, collapse or healing?
escalation: Promptly communicate a femoral-neck tension-side injury, displaced fracture or other high-risk stress fracture.

measurements.pitfall: Apparent change can result from rotation or beam angle.

measurements.name: Articular incongruity
measurements.method: Measure maximal step and gap on the best projection or CT plane.
measurements.pitfall: Do not claim precise articular congruity when overlap or a cast obscures the surface.

pitfalls: A negative initial radiograph does not exclude an occult carpal fracture when clinical suspicion remains.
Describe morphology and displacement even when using an eponym or classification.
impression_prompts: Is the fracture articular and how displaced is it?
Is radiocarpal or DRUJ alignment disrupted?
Is reduction improved and what residual deformity remains?
escalation: Promptly communicate fracture-dislocation or severe malalignment requiring urgent clinical assessment.

protocol: Use a true lateral with the elbow flexed 90 degrees and an AP in extension; a rotated lateral invalidates the fat-pad and anterior humeral line assessment.
Record age, side and injury mechanism; compare with the other elbow only when an ossification centre remains uncertain.

checklist.label: Fat pads
checklist.detail: Look for a visible posterior fat pad or an elevated anterior fat pad as signs of a joint effusion.

checklist.label: Alignment
checklist.detail: Check the anterior humeral line on the true lateral and the radiocapitellar line on every view.

checklist.label: Ossification centres
checklist.detail: Match the visible centres to age in CRITOE order and confirm each is in its normal position.

checklist.label: Fracture
checklist.detail: Name the fracture: supracondylar, lateral condyle, medial epicondyle, radial head/neck or olecranon; describe displacement.

checklist.label: Forearm and associated injury
checklist.detail: Look for a forearm fracture with radial head dislocation, a second fracture and post-reduction alignment.

measurements.name: Elbow alignment
measurements.method: On a true lateral, state where the anterior humeral line crosses the capitellum; state whether the radiocapitellar line passes through the capitellum on each view.
measurements.pitfall: A rotated lateral projection can displace both lines without an injury.

measurements.name: Fracture displacement
measurements.method: Measure fracture gap or translation in mm and describe angulation and rotation, naming the projection.
measurements.pitfall: Lateral condyle displacement can be underestimated on a single view; review the oblique or internal-oblique projection when acquired.

classification.name: Gartland supracondylar classification
classification.applicability: Extension-type supracondylar humeral fractures in children only.
classification.summary: Type I is undisplaced; type II is displaced with an intact posterior cortex; type III is displaced without cortical contact. Describe the displacement directly as well.

pitfalls: A visible posterior fat pad without a visible fracture indicates an effusion and a possible occult fracture; do not report the elbow as normal.
The trochlea does not ossify before the medial epicondyle: an ossicle in the trochlear position without a normally placed medial epicondyle suggests an entrapped avulsed epicondyle.
impression_prompts: Is there an effusion, and which fracture or dislocation is present?
Are the anterior humeral and radiocapitellar lines normal?
Are the ossification centres appropriate for age and in position?
escalation: Urgently communicate a displaced supracondylar fracture, an entrapped medial epicondyle, an elbow dislocation or a radial head dislocation with forearm fracture.

protocol: Start with radiographs of the whole lesion; use CT for matrix and endosteal detail and MRI for marrow extent, cortex, soft tissue and cartilage-cap thickness.
Record age, symptoms at the lesion, known multiple lesions or syndromes, and the date of any comparison study.

checklist.label: Site and matrix
checklist.detail: Name the bone, central or surface location and the chondroid rings-and-arcs matrix.

checklist.label: Endosteal and cortical change
checklist.detail: Describe endosteal scalloping depth and length, cortical thickening, expansion, breach and periosteal reaction.

checklist.label: MRI characteristics
checklist.detail: Assess lobulated cartilage signal, entrapped fat, peritumoral oedema and enhancement pattern.

checklist.label: Soft tissue and cap
checklist.detail: Look for a soft-tissue mass; for an osteochondroma confirm cortical and medullary continuity and measure the cartilage cap.

checklist.label: Growth and grade-relevant features
checklist.detail: Compare with prior imaging and look for a non-chondroid aggressive component.

measurements.name: Lesion size
measurements.method: Measure the longest dimension and two orthogonal dimensions of the chondroid lesion on MRI or CT.
measurements.pitfall: Compare like with like; radiographic and MRI extent are not interchangeable.

measurements.name: Endosteal scalloping
measurements.method: Report the depth as a proportion of normal cortical thickness and the craniocaudal length of the scalloping.
measurements.pitfall: Oblique planes exaggerate depth; measure perpendicular to the cortex.

measurements.name: Cartilage cap
measurements.method: Measure an osteochondroma cap perpendicular to the underlying bone at its thickest point on MRI or ultrasound.
measurements.pitfall: An adjacent bursa or perichondrium can be mistaken for cap thickness.

pitfalls: Imaging features of enchondroma and atypical cartilaginous tumour overlap; describe the features that favour one rather than assigning a histological grade.
Deep endosteal scalloping (more than two-thirds of cortical thickness), cortical breach, periosteal reaction or a soft-tissue mass favour a higher-grade tumour and warrant specialist referral.
impression_prompts: Is this a chondroid lesion, and is it central or surface?
Which features favour enchondroma, atypical cartilaginous tumour or higher-grade chondrosarcoma?
Is follow-up, specialist bone-tumour review or no further imaging appropriate?
escalation: Expedite specialist review for an aggressive chondroid lesion, a lytic non-chondroid component or a pathological fracture.

protocol: Review thin-section CT with sagittal and coronal reformats for fracture morphology; use MRI for the posterior ligamentous complex, cord, conus and epidural space when acquired.
Count levels from a documented reference and record the clinical neurological status supplied, because TLICS includes it.

checklist.label: Level and alignment
checklist.detail: Identify each injured level and describe kyphosis, translation or rotation.

checklist.label: Fracture morphology
checklist.detail: Classify the vertebral body injury as compression, split, incomplete or complete burst, and assess the posterior wall.

checklist.label: Posterior ligamentous complex
checklist.detail: Assess interspinous widening, facet diastasis or dislocation and MRI signal in the supraspinous and interspinous ligaments and ligamentum flavum.

checklist.label: Canal and neural elements
checklist.detail: Describe retropulsion, canal compromise, epidural haematoma and cord, conus or cauda equina findings.

checklist.label: Classification and other injuries
checklist.detail: Give AO type and TLICS imaging components, and survey for non-contiguous fractures and paraspinal injury.

measurements.name: Fracture deformity
measurements.method: Measure anterior and posterior vertebral height loss, local kyphosis with named endplates and translation in mm.
measurements.pitfall: State the reference levels; different angle methods are not interchangeable.

measurements.name: Canal compromise
measurements.method: Measure retropulsed fragment depth and residual canal diameter on axial CT at the level of maximal narrowing.
measurements.pitfall: Canal narrowing on CT does not by itself establish neurological injury.

classification.name: AO Spine thoracolumbar / TLICS
classification.applicability: Acute thoracolumbar fractures. TLICS requires the clinical neurological status as well as imaging.
classification.summary: AO type A compression (A0–A4), B tension-band (B1–B3) and C translation injuries. TLICS scores morphology, posterior ligamentous complex integrity and neurological status; do not complete the neurological component from imaging alone.

pitfalls: A burst fracture with an intact posterior ligamentous complex differs from a tension-band injury; look specifically for posterior distraction.
Non-contiguous spinal fractures are common in high-energy trauma; survey the whole imaged spine.
impression_prompts: Which level is injured and what is the fracture morphology?
Is the posterior ligamentous complex or tension band disrupted?
Is there canal compromise or neural compression, and are there other fractures?
escalation: Immediately communicate a translation or distraction injury, cord or cauda equina compression, or an unstable fracture pattern.
